Before starting, read the OpenTelemetry project contribution guide (community/guides/contributor)
Select an issue from the "Good First Issue" and "Help Wanted" issue search links (ordered by difficulty/complexity)
Comment on the issue you want to work on so it can be assigned to you
For work not listed as an issue (new feature/enhancement), first read docs/vision.md, then create an issue describing the proposal in advance
Reference to the internal architecture documentation (docs/internal-architecture.md) for newcomers
Fork instructions: click the 'Fork' button and clone with `git clone git@github.com:USERNAME/opentelemetry-collector.git`
Add the upstream remote: `git remote add upstream https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector.git` and verify with `git remote -v`
Update your fork with `git fetch upstream`, `git checkout main`, `git merge upstream/main`; always work in a branch of your local copy
Link to the general contributing guide's GitHub workflow section
Required tools list: Git, Go (version declared in the relevant go.mod or newer), GNU Make, Docker, and the OpenSSL Library (for the `config/configtls` component)

Repository setup: clone upstream with `git clone git@github.com:open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector.git`, then `cd opentelemetry-collector` and `git remote add fork git@github.com:YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/opentelemetry-collector.git`
Run tests, fmt, and lint with `make`; run `make markdownlint` to check Markdown formatting
Creating a PR command sequence: `git checkout -b feature`, edit, `make`, `make fmt`, `git commit`, `git push fork feature`

Commit message guidance: use descriptive messages (link to cbea.ms recommendations), GitHub copies commit messages into the PR description, squash into a single commit before creating the PR, and maintainers must edit the concatenated squash message before merging

General notes: the project uses Go 1.25.x and GitHub Actions; the exact minimum supported patch version is defined by the repository's `go.mod` files and may increase within a supported Go minor version
Recommendation to run `make gofmt all` before submitting a PR
Two changelogs exist: `CHANGELOG.md` for collector users (behavior changes) and `CHANGELOG-API.md` for developers importing packages
Changelog entry required for: behavior changes of a component, configuration changes, changes to default settings, new components, and changes to exported elements of a package
Changelog entry may be omitted for: test updates for flakiness/coverage, CI/CD process updates, and internal package updates; when uncertain, add an entry

Changelogs are autogenerated from `.yaml` files in the `./.chloggen` directory; the file name must be unique since the last release; during the release process all `./chloggen/*.yaml` files are transcribed and then deleted

Changelog steps: `make chlog-new` to create the entry file (named from your branch, e.g. `./.chloggen/my-branch.yaml`), fill in all fields, run `make chlog-validate`, then commit and push; alternatively copy `./.chloggen/TEMPLATE.yaml`

Local testing: run commands from the repo root, build with `make otelcorecol`, run `./bin/otelcorecol_<os>_<arch> --config ./examples/local/otel-config.yaml` (binary name depends on platform, e.g. `./bin/otelcorecol_darwin_arm64`), and verify the changes are reflected
Contributing images: use Excalidraw and tick the "Embed scene into exported file" option when exporting so the image remains editable
Common issues: build failures from dependency/pseudo-version errors; `go env GOPROXY` should return `https://proxy.golang.org,direct`, otherwise set `export GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct`

Makefile guidelines: the root `Makefile` SHOULD contain repo-level targets, `Makefile.Common` SHOULD contain module-level targets, and each module should have a `Makefile` at its root that includes `Makefile.Common`

Module-level targets SHOULD NOT act on nested modules (e.g. `make lint` at the repo root only evaluates `go.opentelemetry.io/collector`, excluding nested modules like `go.opentelemetry.io/collector/component`)
Each module-level target SHOULD have a corresponding repo-level target (e.g. `make golint` runs `make lint` in each module); the root Makefile has "for each module" wrapper targets

Justifications for standalone repo-level targets: target applies to the whole repo (e.g. building the collector), problematic inter-module interaction, tools without scoping (e.g. `porto`), and incomplete coverage from the "for each module" pattern

Default target guidance: the default module-level target should run a substantial set of module-level targets (ideally all, with exceptions for latency), and the default repo-level target should meaningfully validate the entire repo

OTLP protocol version update steps: edit the top-level Makefile's `OPENTELEMETRY_PROTO_VERSION`, run `make genproto`, inspect `pdata/internal/data/protogen`, update `pdata/internal/cmd/pdatagen/internal` for new fields, run `make genpdata`, inspect `pdata/*`, run `make genproto-cleanup`, and update the supported OTLP version in README.md

dropped.item: Module versioning and schema section: versioning of this project is idiomatic of a Go project using Go modules (link to https://golang.org/ref/mod#versions)
Semantic import versioning (link to golang/go wiki Modules#semantic-import-versioning) will be used, and versions comply with semver 2.0 (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html)

For a module at v2 or higher, the major version must be included as `/vN` at the end of module paths in `go.mod` files (e.g., `module go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2`, `require go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2 v2.0.1`) and in the package import path (e.g., `import "go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2/component"`), including in `go get` commands (e.g., `go get go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2@v2.0.1`) — note both `/v2` and `@v2.0.1`
For a module at v0 or v1, do not include the major version in either the module path or the import path

Semantic convention packages contain a complete version identifier in their import path to enable concurrent use of multiple convention versions in a single application; this identifies the specification version used to generate the package and is unrelated to the containing module's version
A single module should exist, rooted at the top level of the repository, containing all packages provided for use outside the repository

Additional modules may be created in the repository to isolate build-time tools, other commands, or independent libraries; such modules should be versioned in sync with the `go.opentelemetry.io/collector` module

Experimental modules under active development are versioned with major version `v0` to imply the semver stability guarantee (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html#spec-item-4), quoted as: "Major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development. Anything MAY change at any time. The public API SHOULD NOT be considered stable."

Versioning of the associated contrib repository (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib) is idiomatic of a Go project using Go modules, uses semantic import versioning, and complies with semver 2.0

Contrib v2+ example paths: `module github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/processor/k8sprocessor/v2`, `require .../k8sprocessor/v2 v2.0.1`, `import ".../processor/k8sprocessor/v2"`, and `go get .../processor/k8sprocessor/v2@v2.0.1`; for v0 or v1 omit the major version from module and import paths
In contrib, modules are used to encapsulate receivers, processors, exporters, extensions, connectors and any other independent sets of related components
Contrib experimental modules start versioning at `v0.0.0`, increment the minor version for backwards incompatible changes and the patch version for backwards compatible changes
Mature modules with a guaranteed stable public API are versioned with major version `v1` or greater
All stable contrib modules of the same major version as this project use the same entire version

Stable modules may be released with an incremented minor or patch version even when the module's code has not changed, where the only change is an update of the module's dependency on this project's stable APIs
Contrib modules will be kept up to date with this project's releases
GitHub releases will be made for all releases
Go modules will be made available at Go package mirrors
